it had the servants counted as masters; the verse has the servants counting their masters worthy of honor

actions.new_text: Reckoning something or someone as a certain thing: how a person or thing is counted, judged or esteemed. Sarah counts the promiser faithful, Abraham concludes that God can raise the dead, Moses counts the reproach of Christ greater than treasure, rulers are held to be rulers, the silent fool is held wise, silver is counted as nothing, the men are counted reliable, the people are counted as foreigners, as sheep, as pots, the laws as strange, the potter as clay, the disciples dispute who is held greatest, the uncircumcised is counted as circumcised, those under the yoke count their masters worthy of honor, the Lord counts the exiles good. The word is a reckoning or valuation, the standing given by a judgment. Verses: 1Ki 10:21, 2Ch 9:20, Neh 13:13, Pro 17:28, Mar 10:42, Heb 11:11, Heb 11:19, Heb 11:26, Lev 19:23, 1Sa 1:16, Jer 24:5, 1Cor 4:1, 2Th 3:15, 1Ti 6:1, 1Pe 5:12, Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Isa 29:16, Isa 29:17, Lam 4:2, Hos 8:12, Luk 22:24, Rom 2:26, Rom 8:36.
actions.checked: 1Ti 6:1 (bondservants regard their own masters as worthy of all honor)
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it had the servants counted as masters; the verse has the servants counting their masters worthy of honor

observations.why: it gave the priests as those denied regard; in the verse the priests are denied honor, and the regard withheld is from the scattered

actions.new_text: Having regard: giving notice and heed to someone or something, or refusing it. The Lord has no regard for Cain's offering, the psalmist asks God to have regard for the covenant and the vine, the wicked do not regard the Lord's works, God does not regard those wise in their own conceit, Levi disregards his kin, the righteous have regard for the life of the beast, the Medes have no regard for silver, and the Lord who scattered his people regards them no more. The word is attention that turns toward a person or matter with favor or care, or is withheld. Verses: Gen 4:5, Exo 5:9, Deu 9:27, Deu 33:9, 1Sa 25:25, 2Ki 3:14, 2Ch 5:11, 2Ch 6:19, Job 9:21, Job 34:27, Job 35:13, Job 37:24, Psa 28:5, Psa 74:20, Psa 80:14, Psa 119:117, Psa 144:3, Pro 12:10, Isa 5:12, Isa 13:17, Isa 33:8, Lam 4:16.
actions.checked: Lam 4:16 (he will regard them no more; no honor was shown to the priests)
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it gave the priests as those denied regard; in the verse the priests are denied honor, and the regard withheld is from the scattered

it counted H3820A among the small words; in 1Sa 25:25 the heart is the word of the idiom that the English renders regard

actions.new_text: The surface regard carries over twenty codes in three uses. Of looking and heeding: H8159 in Gen 4:5, Exo 5:9 and Psa 119:117, H5027, H7200G, H6437G, H7789, H0995 in Psa 28:5, H7919A, H6485I, H3045, H8104J, and H5375Q in 2Ki 3:14 (to lift the face). Of counting as something: H2803H, H5234A, H5414I, H6188 in Lev 19:23, G3049, G2233, and G6063 with G1097 in 2Cor 5:16. Of a link of respect: H9006 in Judg 15:3, H1700 in Ecc 3:18, G4012 in Act 28:22, G3313 in Col 2:16. H0408, H3808 and H0853 are small words in the units; H3820A (heart) carries the idiom of setting the heart in 1Sa 25:25.
